video_title: 🎃 Stories for Kids Read Aloud for FALL HALLOWEEN 🎃 Pick a Pumpkin Mrs. Millie [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]
summary_text: Mrs Milly takes her class on a visit to Farmer Don’s pumpkin patch, but she keeps saying the wrong words. The children laugh and correct her when she says things like “mice” for nice, “pumpkin pets” for pumpkin patch, and “jackals” for jackets. They ride the bus to the farm and meet Farmer Don at the gate. Mrs Milly calls the wagon a Dragon and the scarecrow a haircrow, while the children know the correct words. The class walks through the muddy field, picks round orange pumpkins, and loads them into the wagon. Then they visit the barn, feed the horses, toss grain to the chickens, and see Mrs Milly take a picture of the pigs. She also says “pet the boats,” “snake the leaves,” and “hide and sheep hide and seek,” and the children keep fixing her words. After drinking apple cider, they return to school with their pumpkins and say goodbye to Farmer Don and his goats.

video_title: READ ALOUD: Love Monster
summary_text: Love Monster, written and illustrated by Rachel Bright, is about a monster living among many cute fluffy animals. The monster is not cute and fluffy himself. He is a little funny-looking, slightly hairy, and googly-eyed, so he does not seem to fit in with the kittens, puppies, and bunnies around him. He feels sad, but he does not keep moping. Instead, he goes out to look for someone who will love him just the way he is. He searches high and low, and even middle-ish, and he looks inside and outside more than once. He keeps thinking he has found the right place or person, but each time he finds out that things are not what they seemed. The search goes badly for a long time, and then it becomes dark and scary. The monster loses his oomph and decides to give up and go home. Right then, when he does not expect it, love finds him.

video_title: 💦 Mrs. McNosh Hangs Up Her Wash 💦| Read Aloud for Kids!
summary_text: On Monday mornings, Mrs. Nelly McNauch does her wash. She brings out a barrel at dawn and washes all morning long. The postman comes, and she hangs up the mail. She keeps hanging until every last thing in sight is up, even the turkey she is roasting for supper. By dusk, Mrs. Nelly McNaught is finished. She takes off her apron, lets down her hair, and hangs herself up in a comfortable chair.

summary_text: On Christmas Eve, the family goes to Luke's forest to get their tree. They ride in the truck through the Christmas lights and into the dark woods. Nina is nearly asleep, and Dad rolls down the windows so everyone can smell the tree smell. In the forest, Dad leads the way with a lantern, Mom and Nina walk together, and the child follows with a blanket. A deer looks at them and runs away. Then Dad finds the tree they always use. The family decorates it with a popcorn chain, fruit, and homemade food balls, and they put nuts and crumbs on the ground for little animals. Mom gives them hot chocolate, and they wait quietly for animals to come, but none do. Dad says the tree is shy, and Nina says she is shy too. They sing Christmas songs, leave the forest, and go home. Nina gets too tired to walk, so Dad carries her. Later, the child lies in bed and thinks about the tree and the animals that might come to celebrate there on Christmas day.

video_title: GIRAFFE PROBLEMS by Jory John | Read Aloud by Erika Moondoodlez
summary_text: Edward the turtle keeps saying he feels bad about his neck. He thinks it is too long, too bendy, and too easy for everyone to stare at. He tries many ways to hide it, including scarves, ties, shrubs, trees, ditches, and the river. He also looks at other animals and compares his neck to a zebra’s, an elephant’s, and a lion’s. Edward remembers that his mother told him to be proud, but he still feels unhappy. Then he meets Cyrus the giraffe, who says he has been waiting seven days for a banana on a hill to turn yellow. Cyrus says he wishes he had Edward’s neck, because it would help him reach things. Edward helps Cyrus get the banana, and Cyrus finally eats it. Cyrus thanks Edward and says his neck is elegant. Edward and Cyrus then talk about bow ties and both feel good about their necks.

video_title: Snowflake Bentley
summary_text: Wilson Bentley, known as Willie, was born in Vermont where winter snow was common. As a boy, he loved watching snowflakes fall and wished he could save their beauty. His mother taught him at home, and when she gave him a microscope, he used it to study snow crystals. He discovered that the crystals had six branches and that no two were the same. Willie first tried to draw the snowflakes, but they melted before he could finish. Then he learned about a camera that could take close pictures. His parents spent their savings to buy it, and Willie worked hard even when the first photographs failed. After many tries, he found a way to photograph snowflakes by using a small lens opening and long exposure. He also learned how to make the crystals show more clearly. Willie kept working through many winters, making pictures, giving talks, and sharing them with children, adults, and schools. He became famous as the snowflake man, published Snow Crystals, and later died after walking home in a blizzard and becoming ill with pneumonia.

video_title: I Am Rosa Parks - Read Along w/ Words on Screen
summary_text: Rosa Parks learned as a child to respect herself and expect respect from others. When a white boy on rollerskates shoved her, Rosa pushed him back and calmly explained what happened to his angry mother. She faced unfair treatment because she was Black. Black people had separate neighborhoods, restaurants, bathrooms, elevators, and water fountains. Their schools were smaller and poorer, and Black children had to walk while white children rode buses. On a bus, a driver once forced Rosa to leave because she entered through the front. As an adult, Rosa worked as a seamstress and helped the NAACP fight unfair laws. One day in Montgomery, Alabama, the same driver ordered her to give up her seat to a white passenger. Rosa stayed seated because she was tired of giving in. She was arrested, and the Montgomery bus boycott lasted 381 days. The rules changed, and buses could no longer separate people by race. Rosa said ordinary people can stand up for justice together.

summary_text: The Cat in the Hat takes Sally on a trip through the rain forest and teaches about its four layers. He says rain forests are found near the equator and get lots of rain. He also names seasonal rain forests, cloud rain forests, and mangrove rain forests. Then he explains transpiration, which helps create rain when plants release water and warm air rises into clouds. The first stop is the emergent layer, where trees grow very tall and use buttress roots for support. Harpy eagles and macaws live there. Next is the canopy, where epiphytes grow and animals such as howler monkeys, sloths, toucans, tree frogs, and hummingbirds find food. The third layer is the understory, where not much sunlight reaches and spider monkeys and ocelots live among vines and ferns. The last layer is the forest floor, where there is leaf litter and animals like jaguars, snakes, insects, and spiders. Human people also live there. In the end, the Cat says the rain forest is being cut down and tells people to save the trees.
